title: Passing Network Analysis for the Huskies
source_quality: 24-page PDF, text layer mostly readable except private-use subscript glyphs on pages 9-12 and replacement characters on page 10.  Appendix R and Matlab code present but contains errors (size=4, hard-coded core list).  All figures and tables readable from raster.

official_requirements: Identify network properties from the passing data
Determine indicators of team success and model team performance
Create a model of team play for prediction
Recommend strategies for the Huskies to improve
task_reconstruction.paper_approach: Builds a directed weighted passing network per match, extracts five network readings (centroid, dispersion, core-periphery, motifs, degree), defines seven indicators (3 individual + 4 team-level), regresses goal difference on five survivors, keeps three, ranks the team on each, converts rankings to coaching advice, and generalises the four indicators into a teamwork model.
task_reconstruction.paper_coverage: All four requirements addressed; generalisation added as extension.
coverage_gaps: No prediction is made for future matches despite claiming predictive power
The generalised teamwork model is asserted without validation

contributions.summary: Treats a full season of passing data as a single graph object and derives all metrics from it.
Applies spatial dispersion to a passing network centroid as a team spread indicator.
Defines seven indicators spanning individual, spatial and temporal scales.
Screens and regresses indicators against goal difference to identify the three strongest.
Translates regression coefficients into three actionable coaching recommendations.
Maps sport-specific indicators to domain-general teamwork properties.

weak_links: INDICATORS -> GOAL-REGRESSION: pi3 uses core count that disagrees between body (10) and appendix (12)
LOCAL-STRUCTURE -> INDICATORS: motif counts from code use size=4 not size=3

assumptions.summary: A pass is the unit of evidence; other events are excluded.
Each player acts independently of external pressure.
Each match is undisturbed by external factors.
Player position constrains movement and defines the coordinate system.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 23,429 passes across 366 players in 38 matches from one season.
Filter to successful passes; construct directed edge list per match.
Passes with fewer than 10 excluded per player to avoid substitution effects.

models.summary: Directed weighted graph: nodes=players, edges=pass counts, positions=average coordinates.
Equations (1)-(2): centroid as weighted mean, dispersion as weighted std dev.
Core-periphery partition via Ucinet; thirteen three-node motif census.
pi1-pi3 individual indicators; tp1-tp4 team processes; equations (3)-(4).
OLS with robust SE on goal difference; two fits (5-var, 3-var).
Ranks Huskies on extension, configuration, dynamic aspects across 20 teams.

verification.summary: Visual scatter check for each indicator vs goal difference.
F test, R-squared, RMSE, coefficient significance for both fits.
Variance inflation factors for three retained predictors.
Post-hoc correlation check for discarded pi1 (0.32) and pi3 (0.05).

results_trace.summary: model output: regression coefficients -> visual: Figure 9 tables -> interpretation: tp3 and tp4 significant, pi1 negative -> answer: three indicators predict goal difference -> consequence: coaching advice can be issued -> caveat: R2 drops from 0.4656 to 0.4138.

model output: indicator values per team -> interpretation: extension 2nd, config 15th, tempo 7th -> answer: Huskies strong in spread, weak in triadic passing -> consequence: train three-member groups and slow the opening -> caveat: rankings from single season with no uncertainty.

model output: four indicators -> interpretation: mapped to interaction frequency, task coverage, pacing, subgroup communication -> answer: general teamwork model -> consequence: transferable to non-sport teams -> caveat: mapping is asserted, not validated.

writing_logic.summary: Stakes-first pattern: claim needing no data, then route each task by heading word, give advice directly.
World-to-football funnel: global scale paragraph, sport paragraph, client request, task list with added goal.
Reason-tool-display-handoff: for each network object, state the football reason, name the tool, show the figure, hand the quantity forward.
Screen-regress-diagnose: visual scatter screening, stepwise OLS, VIF check. Each phase prunes variables.
Finding-to-instruction: report the coefficient, convert to training practice, name the coach, rank the team.
Mirror pattern: each weakness traces to an assumption; each strength names its supporting evidence.

language_observations.summary: Uses compressed task routing with heading words and colon-separated content blocks; effective for scanability.
Four-move introduction pattern (reason-tool-display-handoff) anchors imported concepts in the problem domain.
Bullet-list indicator definitions with denotation markers; consistent but monotonous voice.
Confuses F statistic with p-value; describes degraded R2 as 'high level'; ad hoc correlation band.
Garbled machine-translation prose that breaks the technical argument.
Restates findings in discovery order; converts negative tempo finding into a rather-than planning rule.

visualization_observations.summary: Fig1/Fig2: directed node-link diagrams with position, size and width encoding pass data effectively.
Fig3: printed integer matrix; auditable but hard to scan without highlighting.
Fig4: Ucinet partition output; truncated, so reader cannot verify full partition.
Fig5: thirteen three-node motif types as visual dictionary; small but functional.
Fig6: bar chart of motif frequencies showing motif 12 dominance.
Fig7: cumulative pass timeline; caption duplicates Fig6 (diagnostic counterexample).
Figure 8: scatter grid for all seven indicators vs goal difference.
Figure 9: both Stata regression outputs with full coefficient detail.
Figure 10: VIF values confirming no multicollinearity.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: C: The clean dependency chain from a single graph object through indicators to recommendations may have satisfied judges looking for a coherent methodology, but the paper alone cannot establish why judges awarded it.
J: The direct coefficient-to-advice trace and the generalisation to non-sport teams may have demonstrated practical relevance, but this is speculative.

weaknesses.summary: Appendix R code uses size=4 and which.max, cannot reproduce three-node motif statistics.
Caption duplicates Fig6; content is a timeline, not a motif chart.
Page 7 prose says 'figure 4' for motifs but they are printed as Fig5.
Variable removal by visual inspection with no formal test.
tp2 kept with p=0.111 in first fit; inconsistent with the 0.05 significance level applied to others.
F statistic described as 'significantly lower than 0.05'; confuses test statistic with p-value.
R2 drops from 0.4656 to 0.4138 but second value called 'high level' without comparison.
Ad hoc band 0.3<0.32<0.8 with no cited source for thresholds.
Garbled machine-translation prose in Configuration section.
Four indicators mapped to teamwork properties without validation.
50-pass threshold for tempo is arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis.
10-pass filter to exclude substitutions is arbitrary.

independent_extensions.summary: Build a time-varying passing network with match-phase segmentation (first half, second half, overtime) and test whether indicator values shift across phases.
Replace the visual scatter screening with a formal variable selection method (LASSO, stepwise AIC/BIC) and compare the retained set.
Correct the appendix R code to use size=3 for the motif census and recompute tp4 across all 38 matches.
Add out-of-sample validation by holding out matches and testing the regression's predictive accuracy on unseen games.
Draw the implicit six-model dependency chain as an explicit diagram and annotate each edge with the transferred quantity and its units.

candidate_rule_impacts.rationale: Second D paper using a network as the sole data object; confirms that edge semantics, demand/flow, and graph transformation auditability are recurring concerns.
Multiple instances of claim-evidence mismatch: R2 degradation hidden, F vs p confusion, ad hoc correlation band.
Scatter screening without formal test, body-appendix code discrepancy, VIF-only diagnostics.
Caption duplication, cross-reference error, garbled prose, duplicated paragraph — all recurrent writing quality issues.
Motif selection and configuration ratio construction from a motif census with reproducibility issues.
50-pass tempo threshold and 10-pass filter are arbitrary with no sensitivity test.

unresolved_questions: Which core player list (10 or 12) was actually used to compute pi3 in the regression?
What R or Matlab code produced the three-node motif frequencies if the appendix uses size=4?
What is the exact standardisation method applied to indicators before regression?
Why was tp2 retained in the second fit despite p=0.111 in the first?
What sensitivity does the 50-pass threshold have on tp3's sign and significance?
Were all 38 matches played on the same pitch dimensions, or does the [0,100] coordinate system normalise different venues?
